title: First Impact: SDK Rapid Ops Lattice
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a compact, telemetry-first SDK quickstart we can ship as a tiny first-run experience for new developers and internal engineers who want a fast proof-of-concept with Redwood Inference. The emphasis: immediate observable wins (latency, cost, token accounting) + a path from zero-config local dev to a reproducible production wiring.

Goals:
- Get a dev from zero to a running sample app with real Redwood requests in under 10 minutes (local mode).
- Surface cost/latency/availability metrics out of the box so users can iterate on prompt/dev tradeoffs immediately.
- Provide three frictionless upgrade paths (local -> containerized -> infra-ready) with small diffs.
- Make a repeatable checklist for SDK maintainers to keep the quickstart up-to-date with API and telemetry changes.

Primary audience:
- Product engineers evaluating Redwood for feature prototyping.
- Internal platform/solutions engineers who need a reproducible demo for customers.
- Developer advocates running workshops and office hours.

Non-goals:
- Not a full reference manual; links to main SDK docs will be provided.
- Not a prescriptive production deployment guide — only a minimal, audited wiring for test infra.

Key principles (lattice):
- Telemetry-first: every sample app must ship with pre-wired metrics and a simple local trace.
- Minimal credentials friction: zero-config mode uses a local sandbox key or emulator.
- Latency-aware defaults: small batch sizes, short prefix caching, streaming examples.
- Observable defaults: per-request token cost and latency printed to console and to a local metrics sink.
- Reversible: every step to production must be a small, reversible change.

Three onboarding paths (conversation flows):
1) Zero-config local (target: 10 minutes)
   - clone repo (one-liner), run `make local-run` (or `npm run dev`)
   - local server starts, seeds a lightweight prompt set, and shows live token + latency counters in console UI
   - uses embedded sample prompt + mocked KV cache but issues real Redwood requests using a developer sandbox key (or local emulator)
   - end state: developer can hit /chat and see a streaming reply with telemetry overlay

2) Containerized sample app (target: 20–30 minutes)
   - single Dockerfile, compose to start local Redis and sample app, env var swap of SANDBOX_KEY -> RDW_API_KEY
   - persistent telemetry: logs forwarded to a local vector/loki stack included in compose file (optional)
   - includes small script to generate synthetic traffic with realistic token distribution to exercise batching and cache hints

3) Infra-ready wiring (target: 1–2 hours)
   - terraform fragment and a prod-ready env example: KMS integration, OIDC auth, metric export to prometheus/grafana dashboard snippet, model pinning and rollout config in yaml
   - ready-made canary rollout guide with traffic split sample and automatic fallback to smaller model variant if latency/SLO breached

Telemetry and metrics (minimal set):
- per-request: model, tokens_in, tokens_out, requested_sequence_length, latency_ms, region, success/error code
- aggregate: p50/p95 latency by route, token cost per minute, cache hit ratio, streaming vs non-streamed percent
- logging: sample payloads (sanitized), prompt version id, SDK version string

Console UX ideas (local):
- colored terminal overlay showing: last 10 requests with token usage, latency sparkline, cost estimate for the session
- ephemeral quick links printed to console (open grafana / open sample trace)
- an "explain cost" command that maps tokens -> estimated dollars using current pricing presets (helpful for product folks)

Presets and ergonomics (opinionated defaults):
- DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPERATURE=0.2 for first-run deterministic results
- BATCH_SIZE=8 for developer envs, auto-scale suggestion for production
- STREAMING_ENABLED=true to show low-latency reply UX
- CACHING_HINT=prefix for conversational flows; enabled by default for repeated prompt templates

Maintenance contract (for DE team):
- Keep quickstart in sync with SDK major releases (automated CI job to smoke test basic flows)
- Weekly snapshot: run synthetic traffic for 10 minutes and assert telemetry schema still matches our dashboard ingestion (CI gate)
- Tag a single owner and a secondary reviewer for any change that touches telemetry or credentials handling

Developer-facing checklist (for inclusion in README):
- [ ] clone repo
- [ ] run `make local-run` (or `npm run dev`)
- [ ] open http://localhost:3000/chat and send a test message
- [ ] verify console shows token/cost/latency overlay
- [ ] try `make gen-traffic` to exercise batching
- [ ] flip env var to point to your own RDW_API_KEY and run the containerized path

Security & privacy notes (short):
- Do not log full prompts by default. Sample logging should redact user PII and secrets.
- Sandbox key has strict rate and data retention policy. Docs must communicate sandbox limitations clearly.
- The infra-ready wiring includes a short KMS/HSM checklist and example IAM roles for minimal privilege.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide if sandbox should allow streaming tokens or return fully-rendered outputs only (privacy vs UX tradeoff).
- Agreement on pricing presets for the cost estimator (product to confirm).
- Which internal dashboard will host the canonical quickstart metrics? (options: DE Grafana namespace vs Showroom cluster)
- Should we include a tiny interactive playground inside the doc that replays recorded traces? (would be nice for demos)

Next steps (concrete):
- Prototype zero-config local: Lina + Jonah (2 days) -> working PoC and a single CI smoke test.
- Deck & script for developer advocates: Marco (1 week) -> 10-min demo script + two slides.
- Telemetry contract PR: Aisha (3 days) -> small spec with telemetry schema and CI validator.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep the sample prompt intentionally simple (todo: pick a small multi-turn helpdesk example)
- Sample app should default to a single route `/chat` and minimal html front-end so non-engineers can demo
- Make the compose file optional but included; some folks prefer pure Dockerfile + run scripts

References / links:
- [internal] quickstart telemetry schema (linked_artifacts above)
- Example starter repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter (PR linked above)

Rough timeline for MVP:
- Day 0–2: local PoC + README + CI smoke test
- Day 3–7: containerized compose + vector/logging + demo script
- Week 2: infra-ready wiring, terraform fragment, grafana dashboard sample

If this looks good, I'll convert the prototype PoC into a single-file tutorial that we can embed in the DE docs site and attach a short codelab for workshop usage.

-- end of draft --
